title: Region-adaptive SLO fallbacks and per-tenant surge windows for Dedicated control planes
creator: Marisol Reyes
description: Background: Dedicated control planes occasionally experience region-localized overloads during large customer bursts and during rolling upgrades. Current isolation mechanisms are coarse-grained and lead to either over-eager tenant evictions or degraded global SLOs. Goal: implement a region-adaptive SLO fallback layer that computes per-region latency and availability budgets, wire in a hierarchy of circuit breakers (region -> rack -> tenant) and introduce per-tenant configurable surge-windows that allow limited burst headroom without triggering system-wide shed. This work targets safe rolling upgrades, faster failovers with predictable tail latency, and minimal customer-visible disruptions.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Kickoff: scoped MVP to region-based SLO evaluator + lightweight circuit breaker with three states (Closed, Open, Probe). Agreed to keep tenant defaults conservative and expose surge-window as opt-in flag for Dedicated customers.

2026-03-02 - Design review: PM and SRE asked for explicit admission-controller metrics and per-tenant circuit breaker history persisted for 48h for post-incident analysis. Action: add sampling to KV cache metrics and a bounded event log in control plane.

2026-03-05 - Spike results: two prototypes tested on staging. Region-adaptive thresholds reduced cross-region failovers by ~35% under synthetic blasts. Observed edge case where slow network partitions caused repeated probe flapping; added exponential backoff to Probe->Closed transition.
2026-03-08 - PR opened: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/5821 (region-slo-evaluator + breaker infra). Requesting infra review from @sre-team and @runtime-plat.

2026-03-10 - Safety checklist: confirmed rolling-upgrade compatibility, no schema changes to persisted tenant metadata, added test harness for simulated multi-region packet loss (see link). Will run chaos test next week.

2026-03-12 - UX/PM feedback: product asked for a Console view for per-tenant surge-window usage and an API to opt a tenant into an emergency override. Created follow-up PM ticket (PM-1421) to own Console surface and audit logging requirements.

2026-03-13 - Current blockers: need final sign-off on default surge-window caps (SRE prefers 5% headroom per tenant) and acceptance criteria for failover time budget (target: < 6s median additional latency during region swap).
